articles.title: Russia says Ukraine rejects local ceasefire in dispute over Kostiantynivka
articles.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry accuses Ukraine of refusing to halt shelling in Kostiantynivka, eastern Ukraine, preventing Moscow from handing over the bodies of fallen Ukrainian soldiers. Russia claims Ukraine rejected a ceasefire offer, hindering humanitarian efforts to repatriate remains. This highlights ongoing challenges and lack of cooperation in managing even humanitarian aspects amidst the intense conflict.

articles.title: Blue Wave: How Israel, Washington and a Guernsey Shell Company Stole Colombia’s Election
articles.summary: On June 21, 2026, Colombia's preliminary election results indicated a lead for far-right candidate Abelardo De La Espriella over his left-wing rival, Iván Cepeda. This critical moment reflects Colombia's evolving political landscape and potential future direction. The final vote count will determine the definitive outcome of this significant electoral contest, which could impact regional stability and international relations.

articles.title: Royal Navy in worst state in centuries – retired admiral
articles.summary: Retired chief of the Naval Staff, Lord Alan West, has stated that the Royal Navy is currently in its worst state in British history, operating the smallest fleet ever. This assessment highlights a significant decline in the UK's naval power and defence capabilities, raising concerns about its ability to project influence and protect national interests on a global scale.

articles.title: How SpaceFields is fuelling Indian rocketry’s liftoff
articles.summary: Apurwa Masook and his friends innovatively constructed their initial rockets using basic materials like PVC pipes and fertiliser-grade chemicals. This pioneering amateur rocketry effort highlights ingenuity and practical scientific application. Such initiatives underscore the importance of problem-solving and technical aptitude, qualities highly valued in SSB aspirants, demonstrating how resourcefulness can lead to significant scientific exploration and development.

articles.title: INS Sanshodhak joins Southern Naval Command in Kochi
articles.summary: INS Sanshodhak, the Indian Navy's fourth Survey Vessel Large (SVL), has officially joined the Southern Naval Command after arriving at its home port in Kochi. This significant induction enhances the Navy's hydrographic survey capabilities, crucial for maritime safety and operations. Its arrival strengthens India's naval presence and contributes to strategic maritime data collection, vital for national security.
